The code checks 'if d_since and today' before comparing d_since > today. This matches the claim. | Verify that the horizon check (d_until - d_since > MAX_HORIZON_DAYS) does not depend on today.

symbols.note: Returns True if today > date.fromisoformat(self.until); returns True on ValueError.

symbols.note: Returns dict with item, why, since, until; optionally who.

symbols.note: Parses raw list into list of Acceptance; validates dates, collects problems; sorts by (item, until, since).

claims.text: Fail closed: anything we cannot fully validate is kept, marked with a ``problem``, and suppresses nothing.
claims.why: The code always appends an Acceptance to out, even for malformed entries, and problems are collected in a string but never used to skip the entry.

claims.text: A typo in an acceptance must never be the thing that makes an island invisible.
claims.why: All entries are included in the output list regardless of validation errors, so a typo does not remove an island.

claims.text: ``today`` binds the horizon to the CALENDAR. Without it the only rule is ``until - since <= MAX_HORIZON_DAYS``, which a pair of dates in 2999 satisfies while suppressing forever; the cap measured the acceptance against itself and nothing measured it against now.
claims.why: The code checks 'if d_since and today and d_since > today' only when today is provided. The horizon check (d_until - d_since > timedelta(days=MAX_HORIZON_DAYS)) does not depend on today.

claims.text: Omitting ``today`` keeps the date-shape and horizon checks and skips only that one, so a caller that genuinely has no clock (``--accept`` validating a candidate before writing it) still gets everything else.
claims.why: When today is None, the condition 'if d_since and today and d_since > today' short-circuits, skipping the future-since check, but other validations (date shape, horizon) still run.

claims.text: Which tree the SNAPSHOT was generated against, versus the one just scanned. Reported, never blocking: a baseline taken one commit ago is not a defect, and a gate that goes red on every commit is a gate people switch off. The consumers that RANK WORK out of these lists are the ones that must fail closed on it -- see :func:`snapshot_freshness`.
claims.why: The code defines freshness as a dict field but contains no logic using it. The claim about behavior and the function snapshot_freshness are not in this chunk.

observations.what: parse_acceptances returns sorted list; sorting key uses (a.item, a.until, a.since).
DriftItem.blocking property: returns False if kind in NON_BLOCKING_KINDS or accepted is True.
DriftReport.blocking property: returns list of items where item.blocking is True.
